fields.meta_title: Microsite Landing Page: 4 Examples to Build | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A microsite landing page gives one campaign a page and an address of its own. See 4 examples and build yours by prompt.
fields.h1: Build a Microsite Landing Page With Its Own Address
fields.hero_description: Build a microsite landing page for one campaign, on its own address, with every signup saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Microsite Needs to Do Its One Job
fields.features_subheading: A microsite landing page sits apart from your main site and serves one campaign. Emergent builds these six parts from one prompt.
fields.feature_1:
An address of its own

Publish the microsite on a subdomain of your brand's domain, or on a domain bought for this one campaign. Emergent includes custom domains, and each one you connect uses credits.
fields.feature_2:
Signups in a table you own

Each signup lands as a row in a database you own, with the form's answers and the time it came in. When the campaign closes, the list stays with you, not with the page.
fields.feature_3:
An end date set on day one

Give the app the campaign's last day, and the morning after, it swaps the form for a short ended note and a link to your main site. Nobody signs up for an offer that is over.
fields.feature_4:
A count for every link you hand out

Put the utm_source tag on each link you share, and the app saves that tag with the signup. Each partner and newsletter then gets its own number instead of one blended total.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts while the campaign runs

Choose who hears what: a Slack message to the organizers when a workshop fills, or a Monday email to each partner with its count. The app sends each alert by Slack or email.
fields.feature_6:
A free start and an exportable codebase

The free tier covers building and publishing the microsite. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep the finished campaign on file after it closes.

fields.tab_content_1:
March 12 swapped the waitlist for a store link

Tidewell Audio built a launch microsite at launch.tidewell.example for one new speaker. Until launch day, the page held a single waitlist form that asked for an email and a color. Of the 412 people who joined, 175 picked Slate and 237 picked Sand. On March 12 the page swapped the form for a link to the store.
fields.tab_content_2:
Type on Screen filled all 40 of its seats

The Quarry Hill Design Summit runs 3 workshops of 40 seats each, and its microsite takes the signups. So far, 81 of the 120 seats are taken and 39 are open. Type on Screen is full at 40, Color Systems has 26 and Grid Basics 15. Once it filled, the app closed its signups and alerted the organizers in Slack.
fields.tab_content_3:
The gift guide retires after December 24

A gift guide has a last day. Fernhollow Candle Co.'s guide runs November 20 to December 24 and lists 6 bundles, each linked to the main shop. Of 2,180 bundle clicks so far, 940 went to the $48 Fireside set. After December 24, the bundles come down and an ended note points visitors to the shop.
fields.tab_content_4:
310 signups from Larkspur, 220 from Oakline

Larkspur Coffee and Oakline Bikes share one bike-to-work week microsite. Each partner hands out a link with its own utm_source tag, and each signup row records the link that brought it in. Of 530 signups, 310 came through Larkspur's and 220 through Oakline's. Every Monday, each partner gets an email with its count.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Microsite Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a microsite landing page that runs one campaign at its own address and closes cleanly on its last day.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the campaign and its last day
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the address before the copy
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write one headline and one action
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the page in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the single thing this microsite exists for, and the date it stops taking signups. Put that date in your prompt from the start, because it decides what the page shows the morning after.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose between a subdomain such as launch.yourbrand.com and a separate domain. A subdomain keeps your brand in the address bar; a separate domain suits a co-branded page that belongs to neither partner.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Lead with what the visitor gets, then give them one form or one button. Leave out the main site's navigation, since every link back to it is a way off the page before the signup.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write the page and its rules in plain English: the seat cap, the end date, who gets alerted. Emergent builds the page and the table behind it, and a follow-up prompt changes either.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Tag every link you hand out
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give each partner and newsletter its own utm_source value, such as larkspur or newsletter4. Then a signup from the Thursday newsletter is counted under newsletter4, not lumped in with everyone else.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open the microsite on a phone, sign up with a test email through a tagged link, and check that the row lands in the table with its tag. Delete the test row before the campaign goes out.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Draft the note the page shows after its last day: one line on what ran, and a link to the main site. A campaign page left up past its date keeps collecting signups nobody plans to answer.

faq_plan.q: What is a microsite landing page?
faq_plan.a: A microsite is an individual web page or a small cluster of pages, and a microsite landing page is the page in it that every campaign link points to. Build one when a single launch or event needs a page of its own.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a microsite landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the campaign and the date it ends in a prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder, and Emergent builds the page and a signup table you own. Then tag the links you plan to share, test the page from a phone, and publish it.

faq_plan.q: Does a microsite landing page need more pages behind it?
faq_plan.a: Not unless the campaign needs them. Add a second page only for something the landing page cannot hold, such as the full schedule for a summit with several workshops. Keep the signup form on the landing page itself, with no extra click in front of it.

faq_plan.q: What should a microsite landing page show before a product is available?
faq_plan.a: Show the product, the date it arrives, and one waitlist form, with nothing to buy yet. Keep the form to an email and one choice like color, and the list will measure demand before launch day. If you only want a brief intro screen before visitors reach your homepage, a splash page does that job instead.

faq_plan.q: Should a microsite landing page use a subdomain or a separate domain?
faq_plan.a: Use a subdomain when the campaign belongs to your brand, and a separate domain when it is co-branded or needs a short address for print. Either works: a microsite's main landing page can have its own domain name or subdomain, and custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which partner sent each signup to a microsite landing page?
faq_plan.a: Hand each partner a separate link tagged with a different utm_source value, then count signups by that value. Google Analytics lists utm_source as the referrer, with examples such as google, newsletter4, and billboard. When a visitor clicks a referral link, the URL parameters are sent to Analytics, which gives you a second count to check the signup rows against.

faq_plan.q: What should a microsite landing page show after the campaign ends?
faq_plan.a: Show a short ended note that names what ran and links to your main site, in place of the old form. Skip the maintenance page for this, since a back-soon message promises a return that a finished campaign will not make.

faq_plan.q: Where do signups from a landing page microsite get stored?
faq_plan.a: In a database you own, when the microsite is built with Emergent: one row per signup. The list outlives the page, and you can take the microsite down after the campaign and keep every row. Built apps also connect to any tool with an API, such as HubSpot, for syncing those rows into your CRM.

faq_plan.q: Can I change a microsite landing page after it goes live?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Describe the change in a prompt, such as a later end date or a fourth workshop, and Emergent changes the page and its table. Keep the form fields the same mid-campaign, and rows collected before and after the edit will still line up.

faq_plan.q: What should visitors see after they sign up on a microsite landing page?
faq_plan.a: Show a thank you page that confirms the signup and says what happens next, such as the launch date or the workshop time. Add one next step that fits the campaign, such as a calendar invite for the summit, and leave the rest of your site off that screen.

plan.angle: No top 10 in the workbook (Wave 3); the AlsoAsked tree asks what a microsite is for and how it differs from a landing page, and the answers that rank stay abstract. This page wins by showing four microsites, each built for one campaign with its own address and its own end: a product launch waitlist, an event with capped workshops, a seasonal gift guide that retires after its last day, and a co-branded partner page that counts signups by the link each partner shares. The mechanism each needs (a launch-day swap, a seat cap, an end date, a source tag) is what template galleries leave out. Splash, maintenance and thank you pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
